description: Resilience and Adaptation in New England (RAINE) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by EPA Region 1 (New England). New England communities can learn from others' planning and assessment experiences, share lessons being learned, discover how to better assist municipalities, and promote collaboration. This database catalogs published vulnerability, resilience, and adaptation plans, reports, and web pages from locations across New England. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Extreme Heat, Flooding – General, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Cultural and Community Services, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
